name: Testosterone propionate

card.summary: A short-acting injectable testosterone ester used medically for androgen replacement and, outside medicine, by people seeking more muscle and a more masculine physique.
card.note: Controlled substance in the US and many countries; non-medical use is illicit and carries hormonal and cardiovascular risks.

quick.overview:
Testosterone propionate is an ester prodrug of testosterone with a short duration of action. Medically it is used for androgen replacement in hypogonadism. In appearance culture it is discussed for its androgenic effects on muscle, body composition and masculine features.

It was synthesised in 1936 and introduced in 1937 by Schering, becoming the first marketed testosterone ester. Longer-acting esters largely replaced it from the 1950s. Early clinical reports date to the 1940s; modern trials focus on other esters.
quick.how: It is given by intramuscular injection in oil; the short ester gives a half-life of around a day. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as one option among testosterone esters, often alongside other compounds. Specific regimens are not described here.
quick.risks: Testosterone products are controlled (US Schedule III). Reported effects include acne, increased body hair, voice changes, aggression, painful injections, and, as with other androgens, suppression of natural testosterone and fertility effects. Forum users also discuss hair loss and fluid retention. It should be used only under medical supervision.

lead: Testosterone propionate is a synthetic androgen and anabolic steroid, the C17 propionate ester of testosterone. It acts as a short-acting prodrug that releases testosterone after intramuscular injection, and it is also known as TP, testosterone propanoate and by the brand name Testoviron [1].

Its appeal for appearance runs through testosterone itself. Androgens drive muscle growth, body hair, a deeper voice and the broader set of masculine features, so people who use testosterone esters in physique-focused communities do so to build a larger, leaner, more masculine body. Medically, propionate has been used as androgen replacement for male hypogonadism, and historically for delayed puberty, some breast cancers in women and menopausal symptoms [1][10].

It was introduced in 1937 by Schering AG and was the main medical form of testosterone until about 1960, when longer-acting esters took over [1]. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing discussion it persists because of its short half-life: users describe it as clearing faster than other esters, and it appears as a component in blended products such as Sustanon and Omnadren [1][12][15].

Research on the propionate ester specifically is largely historical: a 1940 British Medical Journal article on functional impotence, a 1939 veterinary paper in dogs, and later trials of topical propionate in vulvar lichen sclerosus [2][3][8][9]. Broader literature on testosterone and anabolic steroids covers the effects on muscle and the adverse effect profile [10][11].

angle.text: As a testosterone ester it raises androgen levels, which underlie muscle mass, body hair and facial masculinisation. In practice, people use it for physique goals; medical use restores levels in hypogonadism.

paras: Medical use is mainly androgen replacement in male hypogonadism. The drug has also been approved or used for low sexual desire, delayed puberty in boys, breast cancer in women and menopausal symptoms, and it is rarely used today because of its short duration of action [1].

Outside medicine, testosterone and its esters are used for physique and performance. Short-term anabolic steroid use in men has been associated with weight gains of roughly 2 to 5 kg, mainly lean mass, and strength gains ranging from 5 to 20 percent of baseline, according to the general anabolic steroid literature summarised on Wikipedia [11]. Estimates cited there put lifetime use among US adults at one to three million people, mostly non-competitive bodybuilders and non-athletes [11].

Forum material shows how propionate is discussed in these communities: a looksmax.org thread asks about fluid retention when combining it with other compounds [4], and T Nation threads discuss it as an option for people who want to inject more often to keep levels steadier, or who report low SHBG [13][17]. Some TRT patients describe doctors prescribing it as a daily-dose protocol, and others describe blended testosterone products that include it [13][18].

Testosterone acts at the androgen receptor, the same pathway responsible for male puberty. Reported effects of androgen exposure include greater muscle size and strength, increased body and facial hair, deeper voice, oily skin and increased libido [1][10]. In transgender men, testosterone is used as masculinising therapy, producing these changes over months [10].

Not all appearance effects are in the direction users want. Testosterone converts partly to dihydrotestosterone (DHT) and oestradiol, which are linked to acne, scalp hair loss in predisposed people and, at high exposure, gynecomastia [10][11]. T Nation users in TRT and hair-loss threads discuss thinning hair and the use of topical or oral hair-loss medications alongside testosterone, and in some cases stopping therapy because of hair loss [6][7].

Propionate is a prodrug: esterases cleave the short propionate chain to release free testosterone, an agonist of the androgen receptor with strong androgenic and moderate anabolic activity [1]. Oral bioavailability is very low and intramuscular bioavailability very high, so it is given by injection as an oil solution; older forms included an aqueous suspension and buccal tablets [1].

Its elimination half-life is about 0.8 days by the infobox figure on Wikipedia, with the article noting that figures within the page conflict, and the parenteral duration of action is listed as three to four days [1]. By comparison, enanthate has a half-life of about 4.5 days and undecanoate about 20.9 days [1][12]. The short ester is associated with painful injections, a point that recurs in forum discussions [1][16].

Doping-control research shows that an intact testosterone ester in blood is unequivocal evidence of exogenous testosterone, and a randomised study characterised how long injected esters remain detectable in serum and plasma [5].

Testosterone propionate is the 17-beta propionate ester of testosterone, with the formula C22H32O3 and molar mass about 344.5 g/mol. The ester carries a three-carbon straight chain, which makes it among the shortest-acting testosterone esters; its relative testosterone content is about 84 percent by weight [1].

Wikipedia lists propionate alongside cypionate, enanthate, undecanoate and isocaproate as marketed testosterone esters, and notes that several others, such as buciclate and benzoate, never reached the market [12].

Masculinising effects include acne, increased hair growth, voice changes and increased sexual desire; testosterone supplementation may lower the threshold for aggressive behaviour in men [1]. Wider testosterone effects include oily skin, fluid retention and gynecomastia at high exposure, increased haematocrit, worsened sleep apnoea, and possible reversible infertility from suppressed sperm production [10].

Serious effects discussed in the literature include liver toxicity (mainly with oral agents), heart disease, stroke, venous thromboembolism and pulmonary oil microembolism from injectable products; androgens are contraindicated in pregnancy and can worsen benign prostatic hyperplasia or accelerate existing prostate cancer [10]. In February 2025, the FDA removed cardiovascular-risk language from testosterone boxed warnings and added a warning about increased blood pressure [10].

For people using anabolic steroids non-medically, reviews describe unfavourable cholesterol changes, hypertension, left ventricular hypertrophy, suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis with testicular atrophy and reduced sperm production, and psychiatric effects such as aggression, with some of these effects disputed [11]. A user in a T Nation fertility log describes waiting for natural production to return after stopping short-ester injections [19].

Testosterone was identified in 1935 by researchers including David, Dingemanse, Freud and Laqueur, and Butenandt and Hanisch published its chemical synthesis from cholesterol that year [11]. Butenandt and Ruzicka were offered the 1939 Nobel Prize in Chemistry; the Nazi government forced Butenandt to decline and he accepted it after the war [11].

Testosterone esters were first synthesised in 1936, with the propionate the most potent and selected for development. Schering AG introduced it in Germany in 1937 as Testoviron, the first marketed testosterone ester [1]. Human trials with testosterone propionate or methyltestosterone began in 1937 [11]. By 1940 it was reported in clinical use for impotence [2].

Buccal tablets (Oreton Buccal) appeared in the mid-to-late 1940s and Ciba marketed an aqueous suspension by 1950 [1]. Enanthate and cypionate, introduced in the 1950s, largely superseded it, and in the US it is now obtainable mainly through compounding pharmacies [1][10]. Through the late twentieth century, anabolic steroids moved from clinical use into bodybuilding and sport; the IOC banned them in 1976 [11].

Legal status. In the US testosterone and other anabolic steroids were placed in Schedule III by the Anabolic Steroids Control Act of 1990, following the 1988 Ben Johnson doping case, and the 2004 amendment added prohormones [11][10]. Propionate is Schedule III in the US and Schedule IV in Canada; testosterone is Class C in the UK and prescription-only in the EU [1][10]. Non-medical use is generally illegal, and the drug is banned in sport by the World Anti-Doping Agency [10][11].

Use in physique communities. Forum participants discuss propionate as a short-ester option, as a component in mixtures such as Sustanon, whose composition users quote as propionate, phenylpropionate, isocaproate and decanoate, and as a way to reduce hormone fluctuation by injecting more often [15][14][7]. A T Nation poster argues that the fluctuation difference between daily and every-other-day schedules is small, apart from the unesterified or propionate forms, and that frequent shots carry a risk of scar tissue [7]. Another notes that propionate is widely known as painful to inject and that products containing it can cause hormonal swings unless injected often [16].

Prescription culture. Testosterone sales in the US rose from about $324 million in 2002 to about $2 billion in 2012, and a 2015 editorial argued late-onset hypogonadism is overdiagnosed and overtreated; lawsuits by 2014 alleged increased heart attack and stroke rates [10].

Historic clinical reports include testosterone propionate in functional impotence (1940) [2] and a 1939 paper on its use in dogs [3]. A review of androgens in metastatic breast cancer notes that early studies with testosterone propionate showed objective regression rates of slightly more than 20 percent in postmenopausal women, and that later synthetic androgens did not significantly improve on it [20].

Randomised trials of topical 2 percent testosterone propionate versus petrolatum ointment in vulvar lichen sclerosus were run in the 1990s, one enrolling 58 patients over a year of treatment [9][8]. A randomised study of injected testosterone esters characterised their detection windows in blood for doping control [5]. In rats, neonatal treatment of females with testosterone propionate masculinised the sagittalis nucleus of the hypothalamus [21]. Modern controlled trials of the propionate ester for physique outcomes have not been published; general trials of testosterone are summarised in broader reviews [10].

lore.intro: On T Nation and looksmax.org, testosterone propionate is discussed as a short-ester testosterone option, as a component of blended products, and as a reference point for how often to inject. Users also trade accounts of hair loss, fluid retention and injection pain [4][6][16].

claims.claim: Propionate lets users keep hormone levels steadier by injecting often
claims.believers: TRT and bodybuilding posters describe daily or near-daily schedules as a way to avoid peaks and troughs, and some say a doctor prescribed propionate for that reason [13][17].
claims.experts: Wikipedia lists its half-life at about 0.8 days versus about 4.5 for enanthate [1][12]. One T Nation poster argues the fluctuation difference between daily, every-other-day and every-few-days schedules is negligible [7]. No published trial has compared these schedules for physique outcomes.

claims.claim: Propionate is notoriously painful to inject
claims.believers: A T Nation poster calls it notoriously painful and says blends containing it produce hormonal swings unless injected frequently [16].
claims.experts: Wikipedia states that injections are often painful, which it attributes to the short ester chain [1].

claims.claim: Testosterone use can cause or accelerate hair loss
claims.believers: T Nation users report thinning on testosterone and describe stopping therapy or adding hair-loss treatments; one describes another user whose hair was damaged on high propionate with dutasteride [6].
claims.experts: Reviews note that conversion of testosterone to DHT can accelerate baldness in genetically predisposed men, and 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors may prevent or reduce testosterone-related scalp hair loss [10][11].

claims.claim: Fluid retention and bloat can be managed with diuretics alongside other compounds
claims.believers: A looksmax.org poster asks whether a diuretic will handle bloat when combining propionate with other compounds [4].
claims.experts: Fluid retention is a recognised effect of testosterone [10]. No published trials test diuretic use for this purpose in physique users, and combining compounds adds uncertainty.

claims.claim: Short-ester testosterone clears quickly, so natural production recovers fast after stopping
claims.believers: A poster in a T Nation fertility log reports waiting to feel a crash after stopping injections of propionate and another short ester, assuming the drug had cleared [19].
claims.experts: Reviews describe suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis by anabolic steroids, with possible infertility; a short course followed by clomifene or hCG usually restores production, but recovery varies [11].

claims.claim: Controlling oestrogen improves how people feel and look on testosterone
claims.believers: A 1,100-post T Nation thread debates the benefits of estrogen for TRT patients, including dosing frequency and side effects such as hair thinning [7].
claims.experts: Testosterone converts to oestradiol, and gynecomastia at high doses is attributed to this conversion [10][11].

claims.claim: Non-medical steroid use is common and low risk if kept short
claims.believers: Forum users discuss first cycles and low-dose protocols as manageable [16][17].
claims.experts: Reviews link anabolic steroids to cholesterol changes, hypertension, left ventricular hypertrophy, infertility and aggression, with some effects disputed, and they are controlled substances in most jurisdictions [11].
